model.rationale: The district's R+17 lean and a favorable environment point strongly Republican, and Carl's $1.2 million raised plus $547K in outside support dwarfs Jones's $86K. Markets price a Democratic win at just 4%, consistent with a Safe R call.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Jones competitive, or a major scandal or independent expenditure against Carl, would be the first sign of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; fundamentals point clearly one way (post-redistricting), so it is treated as safe for that party.

overview:
Alabama's 1st District is an open seat after redistricting, and its fundamentals lean heavily Republican, with a partisan lean of R+17. Jerry Carl, the Republican, has raised over $1.1 million and holds a large cash advantage, while outside groups have spent more than half a million dollars supporting him. Democrat Clyde Jones Jr. has raised under $100,000 with minimal cash on hand.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the forecast rests on fundamentals, money, and prediction markets, which give the Democrat only about a 4% chance. The race is rated Safe Republican, with modest confidence given the absence of direct polling.
